newsitem.title: POLAND: APPROVAL OF POLAND'S PM SINKS AFTER FLOOD -POLL.
newsitem.headline: APPROVAL OF POLAND'S PM SINKS AFTER FLOOD -POLL.

text.p: Approval ratings of Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz sunk four points to 36 percent in August an opinion poll released on Tuesday showed.

A survey commissioned by the Rzeczpospolita newspaper from the private PBS institute showed 48 percent of those polled dissatisfied with Cimoszewicz's performance, six points more than in the previous poll in July.

PBS said that in July Cimoszewicz saw his critics outnumbering those who approved his performance for the first time since taking office in February 1996 and his popularity took a further dive in the August 9-10 poll.
PBS deputy head Ryszard Pienkowski told Reuters the popularity of Cimoszewicz was harmed by last month's catastrophic floods and criticism of the governent's handling of the relief operations.

"Without doubt it was the flood that made the prime minister's popularity fall as well as a public debate over the government operations and the prime minister's own comments in the media," Pienkowski said.

A PBS pre-election poll released on Monday showed the SLD support falling one point to 25 percent and the grouping slipping behind the opposition Solidarity Election Action (AWS) alliance which gained three points to 28 percent.

But Pienkowski said growing criticism of the performance of Cimoszewicz who also heads the election committee of the ruling Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) would have a limited impact on the SLD's chances in September 21 parliamentary elections.
"I would be very cautious to say whether his (Cimoszewicz's) current standing might affect SLD's chances in the coming election," Pienkowski said.
"The popularity of Cimoszewicz among SLD's electorate has not changed radically and 70 percent of its supporters expressed their approval in August," he added.
